Recipe: Almond briouats.
Only recipe foods: Warqa; Almond; Sugar; Cinnamon; Orange blossom water; Butter; Sunflower oil; Honey; Sesame seed.
How it is cooked and served: Grind the Almond coarsely with the Sugar and the Cinnamon, then work in the Orange blossom water and a little of the Butter to make a thick, crumbly paste. [sesame: Toast the Sesame seed in a dry pan, shaking it often, until they turn pale gold.] Cut the Warqa into strips, brush them with melted Butter, and fold a small spoonful of the Almond paste up in each strip into a neat triangle. Seal the last flap with Butter. Warm the Honey gently. Heat the Sunflower oil in a wide pan and fry the triangles a few at a time, turning them, until golden on every side. Dip each one in the warm Honey for a moment, set it on a rack [sesame: and scatter with the Sesame seed].

Recipe: Arancini al ragu.
Only recipe foods: Butter; Onion (minced); Arborio rice; White wine; Chicken stock; Saffron; Butter; Parmesan (grated); Salt; Ragu; Peas; Mozzarella (diced); Flour; Egg; Breadcrumbs; Sunflower oil.
How it is cooked and served: Warm the Chicken stock in a saucepan until it steams, drop in the Saffron and leave it to turn a deep gold. Keep the Chicken stock hot beside the risotto pan. Soften the Onion in the fat in a wide, heavy pan over low heat, with a little Salt, until it is soft and glassy and has taken no colour. Tip the dry rice into the Onion and stir over medium heat until the edges of the grains turn translucent and the rice is hot. Pour in the White wine and stir until it has been taken up. Add the hot Saffron Chicken stock a ladle at a time, stirring, and give each ladle time to be taken up before the next goes in. Stop when the grains are tender with a firm bite at the centre and the rice is thick and holds a trail, thicker than a risotto for eating. Take the pan off the heat. Beat in the Butter and the cheese until the rice is glossy and clings together. Taste, and add Salt if it needs it. Warm the Ragu in a small pan[peas: , add the Peas] and let it cook gently until [peas: the Peas are tender and] the Ragu is thick enough to hold on a spoon. Leave it to go cold. Spread the risotto thin on a tray, let it cool right down and chill it until it is stiff. With wet hands, press a handful of rice into the palm, set a spoon of the cold Ragu [peas: and Peas] and a piece of Mozzarella in the middle and close the rice over it, into a ball or a cone. Roll each in Flour, turn it through the beaten Egg and cover it in crumbs. Lay them on a tray and chill them for a short while. Heat the Sunflower oil in a deep, heavy pan until a crumb sizzles at once. Fry a few balls at a time, turning them, until they are deep golden all round. Lift them out onto a rack and let them rest briefly, as the centre will be very hot. Pile the arancini on a warm plate and serve while the shells are crisp.

Recipe: Arayes.
Only recipe foods: Pita bread; Minced beef; Onion (minced); Parsley (minced); Allspice; Cinnamon; Black pepper; Salt; Olive oil.
How it is cooked and served: Mince the Onion and the Parsley as finely as you can. Work the beef, the Onion, the Parsley, the spices and the Salt together with the hands until the mixture is even and holds together. Cut round the edge of each Pita bread and open it into layers. Spread the meat mixture thinly over the inner face of one layer, right to the edge, then press the bread shut. Brush both outer faces of each stuffed Pita bread with a thin film of Olive oil. Lay the Pita bread on a hot griddle and press them down gently with the spatula. Cook until the underside is crisp and spotted brown, and check the filling against a trusted guide to doneness. Turn each Pita bread over with the spatula and cook the other face until it is crisp and spotted brown too. Cut each Pita bread into wedges and serve at once while the bread is crisp.

Recipe: Arroz con pollo.
Only recipe foods: Chicken thigh; Olive oil; Salt; White wine; Onion (minced); Garlic (minced); Bell pepper (diced); Tomato (grated); Paprika; Rice; Chicken stock; Saffron; Peas; Parsley (chopped); Lemon (halved).
How it is cooked and served: Season the Chicken thigh all over with some of the Salt. Heat some of the Olive oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the thighs skin-side down first, then on the other side, until they are deep golden. Lift them out onto a plate and leave the browned bits in the pot. Pour the White wine into the hot pot and scrape up the browned bits with a wooden spoon until it has almost gone. Warm the Chicken stock in a saucepan until it steams, drop in the Saffron and leave it to turn a deep gold. Keep it hot. Add the rest of the Olive oil to the pot. Cook the sofrito.onion and the sofrito.bell pepper over a low heat until soft, then the sofrito.garlic, then the grated sofrito.tomato. Go on, stirring now and then, until the water has gone and the paste is dark and jammy. Take the pot off the heat, stir in the sofrito.paprika and put it back at once. Stir the Rice into the sofrito until every grain is coated and hot. Tuck the chicken back in, pour in the hot Saffron Chicken stock, and bring it to a simmer. [peas: Scatter the Peas on top.] Cover with a lid and cook over low heat without stirring until the Chicken stock has been taken up. Check the thickest part of a thigh against a trusted guide to doneness. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for a short rest, then loosen the Rice gently with a paddle. [parsley: Scatter over the Parsley.] Serve [lemon: with the Lemon cut in wedges].

Recipe: Arroz negro.
Only recipe foods: Short-grain rice; Squid (sliced); Squid ink; Tomato (grated); Garlic (minced); Paprika; Fish stock; Olive oil; Salt; Alioli; Lemon (halved).
How it is cooked and served: Heat the Olive oil in the paella pan. Add the Squid and stir it over a medium-high heat until the liquid it gives off has gone and it has taken a little colour. Push it to the edge of the pan. Make a clear space in the middle of the pan. Cook the grated sofrito.tomato and the sofrito.garlic there on a low heat, stirring now and then, until the water has gone and the paste is dark and jammy. Take the pan off the heat, stir in the sofrito.paprika and put it back at once. Warm the Fish stock in a pan until it just simmers, and stir in the Squid ink until the Fish stock is evenly black. Taste the Fish stock and add Salt until it tastes a little strong, as the rice will soften it. Pour the hot black stock into the pan and bring it to a lively boil. Scatter the rice evenly over the pan and stir once to spread it. Cook it at a strong simmer without stirring, then lower the heat as the rice swells. When the Fish stock has almost gone, turn the heat up for a short while until a faint crackle tells you the bottom is crisping. Take the pan off the heat, cover it with a cloth and let it rest. Serve from the pan. [alioli: Put a spoonful of Alioli beside each plate.] [lemon: Put a wedge of Lemon beside each plate.]

Recipe: Asperges sauce hollandaise.
Only recipe foods: Asparagus; Hollandaise; Salt.
How it is cooked and served: Cut off the woody ends. Peel each spear from just below the tip to the base. Boil the spears in well-salted water until the tip of a knife slides into the thick end. Drain them on a cloth and serve them warm, with the Hollandaise beside them.

Recipe: Avgolemono soup.
Only recipe foods: Chicken thigh; Water; Onion (halved); Carrot (large pieces); Celery (large pieces); Rice; Egg; Lemon juice; Salt; Black pepper; Dill (chopped).
How it is cooked and served: Put the chicken, Onion[carrot: , Carrot][celery: and Celery] in the pot with the Water and half of the Salt. Bring it slowly to a simmer, skim off the grey foam, and keep it at a gentle simmer until the meat comes easily off the bone. Check a piece against a trusted guide to doneness. Lift the chicken out onto a board and pour the broth through a fine sieve into a clean pot. Throw away the vegetables. When the chicken is cool enough to handle, drop the skin and bones and pull the meat into small pieces. Return the broth to a simmer, add the Rice, and cook it in the broth until the grains are tender. Take the pot off the heat and let the bubbling stop. Beat the avgolemono.egg in a bowl until pale and frothy, then beat in the avgolemono.lemon juice. Beat in ladles of the hot broth, one at a time, until the mixture is warm. Stir it back into the pot, off the heat, and do not let the soup bubble again. Taste the soup and add Salt, pepper or a little more avgolemono.lemon juice. Stir the chicken back into the soup. Ladle it into warm bowls [dill: and scatter over a little Dill]. Serve soon, and warm it only gently if it must wait.

Recipe: Baba ghanoush.
Only recipe foods: Aubergine; Tahini; Lemon juice; Garlic; Water; Salt; Olive oil; Pomegranate seed.
How it is cooked and served: Set the whole Aubergine straight on a gas flame or a very hot grill and turn them with tongs until the skin is black and blistered and the flesh has sagged. Move them to a bowl and cover it, so that the steam loosens the skin. When the Aubergine are cool enough to handle, pull off the skin and tear the flesh open. Leave it in a colander to let the bitter juice run off. Do not rinse it. Crush the Garlic with a little of the Salt until it is a damp paste. Stir the Tahini and the Garlic paste into the Lemon juice. The mixture will stiffen. Beat in the cold Water a spoonful at a time until the sauce is pale, smooth and loose. Mash the drained flesh with a fork into rough strands, then stir in the tahini sauce until the dip is creamy but still has some texture. Taste, and adjust the Salt and the Lemon juice. Spoon the dip into a shallow dish and swirl a well in the middle with the back of the spoon. Pour the Olive oil into the well [pomegranate-seed: and scatter the Pomegranate seed over].

Recipe: Bacalao a la vizcaína.
Only recipe foods: Salt cod; Water; Onion (sliced); Garlic; Choricero pepper; Stale bread; Olive oil; Water; Salt; Flour; Olive oil.
How it is cooked and served: Put the Salt cod skin side up in a bowl of cold Water in the fridge. Change the Water several times, until the fish has lost most of its sauce.salt and tastes pleasant when a small piece is tried. Soak the dried peppers in hot sauce.water until soft, scrape out the pulp and keep the sauce.water. Cook the sauce.onion and the sauce.garlic in the sauce.olive oil, lid ajar, over a very low heat until soft, sweet and pale. Add the pulp, a ladle of the soaking sauce.water and the bread, simmer until the sauce.onion falls apart, then rub the sauce through a sieve. Season it at the end. Lift the Salt cod out, divide it in portions and pat it dry. Dust the portions lightly with Flour and shake off the extra. Fry the portions in the Olive oil, skin side down first, and turn them once, until they are lightly golden but not hard. Slide the Salt cod into the sauce and simmer very gently, shaking the pan now and then. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. Serve the Salt cod in the sauce in a warm dish.

Recipe: Bacalao al pil-pil.
Only recipe foods: Salt cod; Water; Olive oil; Garlic; Guindilla.
How it is cooked and served: Rinse the pieces of Salt cod, lay them skin side up in a deep dish and cover them with cold Water. Keep the dish in the fridge and change the Water several times, until a flake from the thickest part tastes lightly seasoned. Drain the Salt cod and pat it dry on every side with a clean cloth. Slice the Garlic thin. Warm the Olive oil in the pan on the lowest heat with the Garlic [guindilla: and the Guindilla], until the Garlic is pale gold and smells sweet and has not browned. Lift out the Garlic [guindilla: and the Guindilla] and keep them. Slip the Salt cod into the scented Olive oil, skin side down, with the heat very low. The Olive oil must barely stir. Leave the pieces in it until the flesh turns opaque and a milky liquid starts to seep from the flakes, then lift the Salt cod out onto a plate. Do not salt anything. Let the Olive oil cool until it is just warm and pour it into a jug, leaving the milky juices in the pan. Put the Salt cod back skin side up. Shake the pan slowly in small circles on and off a very low heat, and pour the Olive oil back in a thin thread, a little at a time, as the juices turn pale and thick. Stop when the sauce is creamy and clings to the fish. Here the Olive oil goes back in a little at a time, where the usual card starts with a little Olive oil in the pan. Spoon the sauce over the Salt cod and scatter the golden Garlic [guindilla: and the Guindilla] on top.

Recipe: Bamieh bi zeit.
Only recipe foods: Okra; Onion; Tomato; Garlic; Coriander leaf; Olive oil; Lemon juice; Water; Salt.
How it is cooked and served: Slice the Onion thin. Soften the Onion in a little of the Olive oil in a wide pan, with a little of the Salt, until they are soft and lightly golden. Move them to a plate. Trim the stem caps of the Okra in a shallow cone, so that the pods stay whole and do not seep. Brown the pods in a hot pan with more of the Olive oil, turning them, until they are lightly coloured on all sides. Dice the Tomato. Return the Onion to the pan, add the Tomato and the Water, and bring it to a gentle simmer. Cook until the Okra is tender, shaking the pan now and then instead of stirring, so that the pods do not break. Crush the Garlic with a little Salt to a rough paste. Heat the rest of the Olive oil in a small pan. Fry the Garlic paste until it is pale gold, then add the chopped Coriander leaf and fry only until it wilts and darkens. Stir the sizzling taqliyeh into the pot. Add the Lemon juice, then taste and adjust the Salt. Spoon the Okra into a dish and serve it warm or at room temperature, with bread or rice.

Recipe: Bisque de homard.
Only recipe foods: Lobster; Butter; Onion (diced); Carrot (diced); Tomato paste; Cognac; White wine; Fish stock; Rice; Cream; Salt.
How it is cooked and served: Boil the Lobster in plenty of well-salted water. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. When it is cool enough to handle, take the meat out of the tail and the claws and keep it cold for the garnish. Break the shells and the head into small pieces. Fry the pieces of shell in the Butter over a lively heat until they smell toasted. Add the mirepoix.onion and the mirepoix.carrot and cook until they start to colour. Take the pot off the heat and pour in the Cognac from a ladle. Put the pot back, stand clear and set the Cognac alight. Pour in the White wine and scrape the bottom of the pot as the White wine boils down by half. Add the Fish stock, the Tomato paste and the Rice. Simmer until the Rice is very soft. Blend the soup in short bursts, shells and all, until the shells are crushed and the Rice has thickened it. Press it hard through a fine sieve with the back of a ladle. Strain it once more for a smooth soup. Bring the soup back to a simmer, stir in the Cream and let it thicken a little. Taste it and Salt it. Ladle the bisque into warm bowls and set the pieces of Lobster meat in the middle.

Recipe: Blanquette de veau.
Only recipe foods: Veal shoulder (large pieces); Carrot (peeled, large pieces); Onion (peeled, halved); Bouquet garni; Water; Salt; Mushroom (halved); Pearl onion (peeled); Butter; Flour; Cream; Egg yolk; Lemon.
How it is cooked and served: Cover the veal with cold Water, bring it just to a boil, then drain it and rinse off the scum. Put the veal back in the clean pot with the measured Water, the Carrot, the Onion, the Bouquet garni and the Salt. Bring it to a simmer, skim, and cook very gently, lid ajar, until a knife slides into the meat with no resistance. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. Meanwhile cook the Pearl onion and the Mushroom in a ladleful of the broth in a small covered pan until tender. They must stay pale. Melt the roux.butter in a clean pan, stir in the roux.flour and cook it for a moment without letting it colour. Strain the broth. Whisk enough of it into the roux, a ladle at a time, to make a sauce that coats a spoon lightly. Simmer it gently. Beat the yolks with the Cream. Whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce, then stir the mixture back into the pan off the boil. Heat gently until it thickens a little. It must not boil again. Sharpen the sauce with a few drops of lemon juice, taste it and adjust the Salt. Put the veal, the Mushroom and the Onion into the sauce to warm for a moment, and serve with the Carrot.

Recipe: Bœuf bourguignon.
Only recipe foods: Stewing beef (large pieces); Bacon (lardons); Onion (peeled, diced); Carrot (peeled, sliced); Garlic (minced); Flour; Red wine; Beef stock; Bouquet garni; Pearl onion (peeled); Mushroom (halved); Butter; Sunflower oil; Salt; Black pepper.
How it is cooked and served: Put the lardons in a cold, heavy pot over medium heat. Let the fat run, brown them and lift them out. Dry the beef well and Salt it. Brown it in the bacon fat and the Sunflower oil over high heat, a few pieces at a time, until deep brown on all sides. Lift each batch out. Lower the heat. Soften the Onion and the Carrot in the pot, then stir in the Garlic. Put the beef back, scatter the Flour over everything and stir over the heat until no white shows. Pour in the Red wine and scrape the bottom of the pot clean. Add the Beef stock, the Bouquet garni and the lardons. The liquid should barely cover the meat. Bring it to a bare simmer, cover, and cook in a low oven until a fork slides into the beef with no resistance. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. Near the end, brown the Pearl onion and then the Mushroom in the Butter in a frying pan. Lift the beef out. Skim the fat from the liquid, take out the Bouquet garni, and boil the sauce down, if it is thin, until it coats a spoon. Taste and season. Put the beef back with the Onion and the Mushroom and warm it gently. It is better still the next day.

Recipe: Bœuf miroton.
Only recipe foods: Boiled beef (sliced); Onion (peeled, sliced); Butter; Flour; Red wine vinegar; Beef stock; Breadcrumbs; Salt; Black pepper.
How it is cooked and served: Cook the Onion in the Butter with the Salt over medium-low heat, stirring now and then, until soft and golden brown. Scatter the Flour over the Onion and cook it, stirring, until it has turned light brown and smells of toasted nuts. Add the vinegar and scrape the pan as it boils away almost to nothing. Stir in the Beef stock a little at a time, with the Black pepper. Simmer until the sauce coats a spoon lightly. Spread a little of the sauce in a baking dish. Lay the slices of beef on it, overlapping, and cover them with the rest of the sauce. Scatter with the Breadcrumbs. Bake in a hot oven until the sauce bubbles at the edges and the top is golden.

Recipe: Bouillabaisse.
Only recipe foods: Rockfish (large pieces); Monkfish (large pieces); Conger eel (large pieces); Red mullet; Potato (sliced); Onion (sliced); Fennel (sliced); Garlic; Tomato (chopped); Saffron; Orange; Olive oil; Water; Salt; Baguette; Rouille.
How it is cooked and served: Soften the Onion, the Fennel and the Garlic in the Olive oil in the stockpot, without colour, until they are limp and sweet. Add the Rockfish with its head and bones, the Tomato, the Saffron, a strip of the Orange peel and the Water. Bring to the boil, then keep at a lively simmer and skim off the foam that rises. Pour the broth through a fine sieve into the saucepan, pressing the solids with the back of a ladle to take every drop. Throw the bones and the pulp away. Return the broth to a simmer, taste it and correct the Salt. Peel the Potato and slice them thick, all to one size. Lay the Potato slices in the broth. Keep it at a simmer until a knife slips into a slice with a little resistance. Lay the firm fish.monkfish and the firm fish.conger eel in the broth, which must cover them, and simmer briskly. They go in first because their flesh is the firmest. Add the Red mullet last, because its flesh is the most delicate, and simmer only a short while. Lift the fish out with the slotted spoon as soon as it is firm. Toast the slices of Baguette under the grill until they are crisp and pale gold on both sides. Ladle the broth into warm bowls and serve the fish and the Potato on a platter beside it. Serve the toasts and the Rouille at the table, so that each person spreads a toast with Rouille and floats it on the broth.

Recipe: Brochet au beurre blanc.
Only recipe foods: Pike; Court-bouillon; Beurre blanc.
How it is cooked and served: Lay the fish in a pan that holds it snugly and cover it with the cold Court-bouillon. Bring it slowly to a bare tremble and poach until the flesh comes away from the bone. The time counts from the first tremble. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. Lift the fish out, drain it well and take off the skin. Serve it on hot plates with the Beurre blanc spooned over. Make the sauce while the fish poaches: it does not wait.

Recipe: Turkish bulgur pilaf.
Only recipe foods: Coarse bulgur; Onion; Tomato paste; Butter; Water; Salt.
How it is cooked and served: Dice the Onion small. Melt the Butter in a pan over a gentle heat and soften the Onion without colour. Stir in the Tomato paste and fry it until the colour deepens. Recipe: Crêpes Suzette.
Only recipe foods: Flour; Milk; Egg; Butter; Salt; Sugar; Water; Butter; Orange; Cognac.
How it is cooked and served: Whisk the crepe.flour, the crepe.egg and the crepe.salt, then whisk in the crepe.milk and the melted crepe.butter a little at a time until the batter is smooth and as thin as pouring cream. Rest it, then cook thin crepes in a hot buttered pan, a ladle at a time, turning each once. Stack them as they are done. Melt the Sugar with the Water in a small pan over a medium heat, without stirring, until it is a pale amber. Take it off the heat. In a wide pan, stir the juice of the Orange, a little of the zest and the Butter into the caramel and simmer until syrupy. Fold each crepe in half and in half again and lay them in the sauce, spooning it over and turning them once. Warm the Cognac in a small pan, take the wide pan off the heat and pour the Cognac around the edge. Stand back and light it, and spoon the burning sauce over the crepes until the flame dies. Serve at once.

Recipe: Croque madame.
Only recipe foods: Sandwich bread; Butter; Béchamel; Ham; Gruyère (grated); Egg.
How it is cooked and served: Spread part of the Butter on one side of each slice of bread. Lay half of them, buttered side down, on a baking sheet. Spread them with a little Béchamel, then add the Ham and half the cheese. Close with the other slices, buttered side up. Bake until the bread is crisp and golden underneath. Spread the tops with the rest of the Béchamel and cover them with the rest of the cheese. Put them under a hot grill until the top is blistered and golden. While the sandwiches brown, melt the rest of the Butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Break in the Egg and fry them gently, without turning, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft. Slide a fried Egg onto each sandwich and serve at once.

Recipe: Croquetas de jamón.
Only recipe foods: Butter; Onion (minced); Flour; Milk; Serrano ham (chopped); Nutmeg; Flour; Egg; Breadcrumbs; Sunflower oil.
How it is cooked and served: Melt the paste.butter in a wide pan and soften the paste.onion in it without colour. Stir in the paste.flour, then the chopped ham. Beat in the warm paste.milk a little at a time until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the pan in one mass. Season with paste.nutmeg. Spread it in a shallow dish, press a sheet of film onto it and chill it until it is firm all the way through. Beat the Egg in a shallow dish. Roll spoonfuls of the cold paste between floured hands into short logs. Roll each in Flour, turn it through the Egg and cover it all round in crumbs. Lay them on a tray and chill them for a short while. Heat the Sunflower oil until a crumb dropped in sizzles at once. Fry a few croquetas at a time, turning them, until they are deep golden. Lift them out onto a rack and serve hot.

Recipe: Cucumber raita.
Only recipe foods: Plain yogurt; Cucumber (sliced); Cumin; Salt; Mint.
How it is cooked and served: Rub the Cucumber slices with a little of the Salt, leave them to wilt, then squeeze them hard by the handful to wring out the water. Warm the Cumin seeds in a dry pan over a low heat until they darken a shade and smell strong, then tip them out to cool. Crush the roasted Cumin in a mortar to a coarse powder. [mint: Chop the Mint leaves fine.] Whisk the cold Plain yogurt until it is smooth and creamy. Stir in the Cucumber, most of the Cumin and the rest of the Salt. Taste, and chill until it is served. Scatter the [mint: chopped Mint and the] rest of the Cumin over the raita.

Recipe: Cuisses de grenouilles à la provençale.
Only recipe foods: Frogs' legs; Flour; Butter; Garlic (minced); Parsley (chopped); Lemon; Salt.
How it is cooked and served: Dry the Frogs' legs well and Salt them. Roll them in the Flour and tap off all that does not cling. Heat the Butter in a wide pan until it foams. Lay the Frogs' legs in with room between them and fry them over a lively heat, turning them once, until they are golden all over. Check the thickest part against a trusted guide to doneness. Add the Garlic and the Parsley and toss everything for a few moments, until the Garlic smells sweet and has not coloured. Squeeze the Lemon over. Serve at once, straight from the pan, while the crust is crisp.
